mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO below 90 for four consecutive months signals a contraction in industrial production, reflecting weakening manufacturing activity and reduced corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST of more than 1% indicates a broad-based weakening in economic activity and housing demand, which reduces corporate earnings and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline > 1% monthly
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of co-triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in FEDFUNDS of more than 0.75 percentage points, combined with a concurrent rise in CPIAUCSL above 3%, signals aggressive monetary tightening amid high inflation, which increases recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS change > 0.75% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of co-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in PAYEMS above 0.5% for six consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in RSAFS above 2% for three consecutive months signals a surge in consumer savings, which typically precedes a reduction in consumption and weaker retail sales, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
